svg.aria-label: Where the registers run out, on two machines
svg.title: Where the registers run out, on two machines
svg.desc: Five functions, each needing more values alive at once than the last, are added one lane at a time to a chart of register pressure. On x86-64, with fifteen registers to hand out, the lanes run off the end of the register file at the third function and the marks for values kept in memory start appearing. The chart then rebuilds for aarch64, which has thirty registers, and the same five functions fit until the very last one. Same source, same flags, same compiler, and the only thing that changed is how many registers the machine has.

g.text: p04 keeps 6 values alive at once, and on x86-64 every one of them got a register.
p10 keeps 12 values alive at once, and on x86-64 every one of them got a register.
p14 keeps 16 values alive at once, and on x86-64 1 of them went to memory.
p20 keeps 22 values alive at once, and on x86-64 7 of them went to memory.
p30 keeps 32 values alive at once, and on x86-64 17 of them went to memory.
p04 keeps 6 values alive at once, and on aarch64 every one of them got a register.
p10 keeps 12 values alive at once, and on aarch64 every one of them got a register.
p14 keeps 16 values alive at once, and on aarch64 every one of them got a register.
p20 keeps 22 values alive at once, and on aarch64 every one of them got a register.
p30 keeps 32 values alive at once, and on aarch64 2 of them went to memory.
